answer: When an agent registry assigns each identity a unique reasoning challenge every epoch—imagine proving you can trace a river's path across a terrace landscape using only ivory-colored markers—every sybil must burn fresh inference compute. An attacker spawning a thousand fake agents pays a thousand API calls or GPU-hours per round. The cost scales linearly with fake identities, while honest agents pay once. Defenses stack challenges requiring multi-step logic that can't be cached or parallelized across identities.
